content:
Let

\[
P(x)=(1+x)^{10000}=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}x^k.
\]

Reducing \(P(x)\) modulo \(x^{502}-1\) collects terms whose exponents are congruent modulo \(502\). Thus the remainder is

\[
\sum_{r=0}^{501} S_r x^r.
\]

So to determine which \(S_r\) are divisible by \(503\), we compute this remainder modulo \(503\).

Work in \(\mathbb{F}_{503}[x]/(x^{502}-1)\). Since

\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443,
\]

we have

\[
(1+x)^{10000}=((1+x)^{503})^{19}(1+x)^{443}.
\]

Modulo \(503\), the Freshman's Dream gives

\[
(1+x)^{503}\equiv 1+x^{503}.
\]

Also, modulo \(x^{502}-1\),

\[
x^{503}=x\cdot x^{502}\equiv x.
\]

Therefore,

\[
(1+x)^{10000}\equiv (1+x)^{19}(1+x)^{443}=(1+x)^{462}.
\]

Because \(\deg(1+x)^{462}=462<502\), this is already the remainder modulo \(x^{502}-1\). Hence, modulo \(503\),

\[
S_r\equiv [x^r](1+x)^{462}.
\]

So

\[
S_r\equiv 
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r}, & 0\le r\le 462,\\[4pt]
0, & 463\le r\le 501.
\end{cases}
\]

For \(0\le r\le 462\), the prime \(503\) is larger than \(462\), so it does not divide any \(\binom{462}{r}\). Thus those \(S_r\) are not multiples of \(503\).

For \(r=463,464,\dots,501\), we have \(S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}\), so those are multiples of \(503\).

The number of such \(r\) is

\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
